name: Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata Type 3

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata

criteria.description: Bilateral rhizomelic shortening of the proximal limbs
Epiphyseal stippling (punctate calcifications) visible on radiographs
Deficiency of acyl-CoA oxidase 1 (ACOX1) enzyme activity or related peroxisomal dysfunction
Characteristic facial features including midface hypoplasia and depressed nasal bridge

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of rhizomelic limb shortening, epiphyseal stippling on radiographs, and confirmed peroxisomal enzyme deficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing for ACOX1 mutations can confirm diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral rhizomelic shortening of humerus and femur
searchTerms: both arms and thighs shortened proximally
bilateral rhizomelic shortening of humerus and femur
short upper limbs on both sides
punctate calcifications seen on bone x-rays
spots of calcium in bone ends on imaging

common.symptomName: Midface hypoplasia with depressed nasal bridge
searchTerms: underdeveloped middle face with flat nose bridge
sunken midface and low nasal bridge

common.symptomName: Severe developmental delay and intellectual disability
Joint contractures and limited range of motion

searchTerms: poor growth resulting in short height
failure to grow to normal height

occasional.symptomName: Feeding difficulties and failure to thrive

rare.symptomName: Skeletal dysplasia beyond rhizomelia (e.g., metaphyseal abnormalities)
searchTerms: skeletal abnormalities beyond proximal limb shortening
bone growth disorders with metaphyseal changes
generalized skeletal dysplasia with bone deformities

laboratory: Elevated phytanic acid and pristanic acid levels in plasma
Peroxisomal enzyme assay showing ACOX1 deficiency
imaging: MRI brain may show delayed myelination
other: Ophthalmologic exam confirming bilateral congenital cataracts
Audiologic testing indicating sensorineural hearing loss

distinguishingFeatures: Deficiency of PEX7 gene rather than ACOX1
Additional systemic involvement including adrenal insufficiency
Similar clinical features but different genetic cause
More severe neurodegeneration and liver dysfunction

redFlags: Severe rhizomelic limb shortening detected prenatally or at birth
Presence of epiphyseal stippling on neonatal radiographs
Bilateral congenital cataracts in a neonate with dysmorphic features
references: Braverman NE, et al. Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata Type 3. GeneReviews. 2020.
Orphanet: Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata Type 3. ORPHA:309803.
